# Claude Recall ### Claude Code Plugin **Persistent memory for Claude Code.** Search, recall, and re-inject context from every session you have ever run, all from inside Claude Code. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@clauderecallhq/cli?style=flat&color=f97316&labelColor=f97316&label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@clauderecallhq/cli) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@clauderecallhq/cli?style=flat&color=f97316&labelColor=f97316&label=downloads)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@clauderecallhq/cli) [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/clauderecall.com-f97316?style=flat)](https://clauderecall.com) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-proprietary-lightgrey?style=flat)](./LICENSE)


100% local. No cloud. No account. No telemetry. Your conversations never leave your machine.

---
## Install From Claude Code, add the marketplace, then install: ``` /plugin marketplace add https://gitlab.com/clauderecallhq/claude-recall-plugin.git /plugin install claude-recall@claude-recall ``` > The `.git` suffix is required — Claude Code git-clones the marketplace. A bare > repo URL without `.git` will not resolve. The MCP server auto-connects. No config files, no JSON editing required. **Requirements:** Node 22 LTS or newer. macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel), Linux x64 / arm64 (glibc), or Windows 10+ x64. Alpine (musl) and 32-bit platforms are not supported. ### Try Pro free for 7 days Pro adds vector search, MCP semantic tools, and the cog-graph. To try it from the CLI in one step (no browser, no card): ``` npm install -g @clauderecallhq/cli recall activate RECALL7DAY ``` You'll be prompted for your email and your trial license activates on this machine immediately. The 7-day clock starts when you activate.
Every Claude Code session you have ever run. Searchable, threaded, re-injectable.

## What you get **MCP server** with 35 tools (13 always-on read, 22 write-gated).
Claude calls Recall as native tools. Searches your history. Pulls context. Decides.

recall context <id> | claude — Claude resumes with full prior context.

Cost analytics. Hover any day. Exact cost. Exact tokens.

Collections. Drag-to-organize sessions across projects.
### Read tools (13, always available) Core: - `list_projects` - every Claude Code project with session/message counts and latest activity - `list_sessions` - recent sessions with alias, tags, message counts; filters: project, tag, date range - `list_tags` - every tag with counts, most popular first - `search` - full-text search across sessions; supports inline #tag-name tokens; BM25 + optional vector fusion - `find_similar_sessions` - find semantically similar sessions using vector embeddings (Pro only) - `semantic_status` - health snapshot of semantic search: model, worker, queue depth (Pro only) - `get_session` - fetch full session metadata and ordered messages - `context_for_session` - render session as condensed markdown, ready to inject - `recall_neighborhood` - bundle parents/children/citations/similar sessions as one budget-bounded markdown blob - `doctor` - read-only health snapshot (db size, WAL, FTS5 fragmentation, integrity check) Threads: - `thread_list` - all threads, newest first; can exclude archived - `thread_get` - full thread detail with every session edge - `thread_for_session` - return non-archived threads referencing a session ### Write tools (22, require `--allow-writes` or `RECALL_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1`) Write tools are rate-limited (default 60/min), zod-validated, and recorded in a local append-only `mcp_audit_events` log. They never delete user data. Tagging (auto-tag agent flow): - `list_sessions_to_tag` - surface untagged or partially-tagged sessions for review - `apply_tags` - add tags to a session (merge-mode, never deletes) Metadata: - `add_tag` - apply single tag; normalized server-side - `remove_tag` - remove tag; recorded in append-only log - `set_alias` - set human-friendly session alias; previous alias archived - `append_note` - append markdown to session note; separated by --- - `create_collection` - create new collection; optional parent, icon, color - `add_session_to_collection` - add session to collection; idempotent - `remove_session_from_collection` - remove session; recorded in append-only log Threads: - `thread_create` - create thread, optionally seed with origin session - `thread_add_session` - attach session; role=origin or child - `thread_set_parent` - change parent within thread; null clears parent - `thread_remove_session` - detach session from thread - `thread_rename` - change thread display name - `thread_close` - mark thread as closed (sets closed_at) - `thread_reopen` - clear closed_at on closed thread - `thread_archive` - soft-delete thread; hidden by default - `thread_merge` - move all edges from source to dest, delete source - `thread_split` - peel sessions into new thread - `sync_active_sessions` - capture every Claude Code terminal currently open in a repo into one thread, so parallel sessions stay organized - `generate_thread_titles` - generate coherent titles for sessions in thread DAG Maintenance: - `optimize` - WAL checkpoint, FTS5 segment merge, planner stats refresh; optional VACUUM ## Skills (8) User-invocable slash commands inside Claude Code: - `/claude-recall:recall [query]` - search past sessions for context relevant to the current task - `/claude-recall:context ` - load one specific past session's transcript as markdown context - `/claude-recall:neighborhood ` - pull a session's parents, children, citations, similar sessions, and bug-pattern matches as a budget-bounded markdown bundle - `/claude-recall:alias ` - set or update the display name for a session - `/claude-recall:tag ` - apply a tag to a session for later retrieval - `/claude-recall:threads-sync` - capture every Claude Code terminal currently open in this repo into one thread, so parallel sessions stay organized - `/claude-recall:thread-scan` - auto-detect threads across historical sessions in this project using a 6-signal deterministic scorer - `/claude-recall:setup` - verify Claude Recall installation and MCP connection
The full-screen terminal UI. Slash to filter, arrow keys to navigate, live preview in the right pane.
## Why a purpose-built tool? People sometimes ask if this is just "Obsidian for Claude Code." It is not. A general note-taking app cannot watch your filesystem for new Claude Code sessions, index session JSONLs into FTS5 + vector search, expose those sessions as MCP tools, or pipe a session back into Claude with one command. Claude Recall is built specifically for the loop you actually run.
Left: Obsidian vault. Right: Claude Recall TUI. Same idea, different tool.
## Privacy

- Bound to `127.0.0.1`. Never on a public interface. - No telemetry, no analytics, no usage tracking. - The only outbound network call from the running daemon is a daily license-revocation check (Pro tier only) that sends just the license key. - Audit log is local. ### Optional vector-search model Vector search uses an on-device embedder (`bge-base-en-v1.5`, ~110 MB) that's opt-in — `npm install -g @clauderecallhq/cli` does not download it. Install on demand: ``` recall semantic install ``` Everything else (sessions, search, threading, MCP tools) works without it. ## Links - Website: [clauderecall.com](https://clauderecall.com) - MCP server docs: [clauderecall.com/mcp](https://clauderecall.com/mcp) - npm package: [@clauderecallhq/cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@clauderecallhq/cli) - VS Code extension: [clauderecallhq.clauderecall-vscode](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=clauderecallhq.clauderecall-vscode) - Source: [gitlab.com/clauderecallhq](https://gitlab.com/clauderecallhq)
